parts.name: Cell wall
parts.fact: The cell wall is a strong outer layer. It supports and protects the plant cell.

parts.name: Cell membrane
parts.fact: The cell membrane is a thin boundary just inside the wall. It controls what enters and leaves the cell.

parts.name: Nucleus
parts.fact: The nucleus holds the cell’s DNA. DNA carries instructions that help the cell work and grow.

parts.name: Chloroplast
parts.fact: Chloroplasts use light energy to make sugar for the plant. Their green chlorophyll catches the light.

parts.name: Central vacuole
parts.fact: The large central vacuole stores water and dissolved materials. When it is full, it helps keep the cell firm.

parts.name: Mitochondrion
parts.fact: Mitochondria release usable energy from food molecules. A cell uses that energy to do its work.

parts.name: Cytoplasm
parts.fact: Cytoplasm is the jelly-like material inside the membrane. Many cell reactions happen there.

parts.name: Cell membrane
parts.fact: The cell membrane surrounds the cell. It controls what enters and leaves.

parts.name: Nucleus
parts.fact: The nucleus holds the cell’s DNA. It helps direct the cell’s activities.

parts.name: Cytoplasm
parts.fact: Cytoplasm is the jelly-like material where the organelles sit. Many cell reactions happen there.

parts.name: Mitochondrion
parts.fact: Mitochondria release usable energy from food molecules. The cell uses that energy to work.

parts.name: Ribosomes
parts.fact: Ribosomes build proteins. Cells need proteins for structure and for many jobs.

parts.name: Endoplasmic reticulum
parts.fact: The endoplasmic reticulum is a network of membranes. It helps make and move proteins and fats.

parts.name: Golgi apparatus
parts.fact: The Golgi apparatus sorts and packages proteins and fats. It sends them to where they are needed.

parts.name: Lysosome
parts.fact: Lysosomes break down large molecules and worn-out cell parts. They help the cell recycle material.

topics.title: Parts of a Plant
topics.alt: Parts of a Plant painted learning picture

parts.name: Roots
parts.fact: Roots anchor the plant and take in water and minerals from the soil.

parts.name: Stem
parts.fact: The stem holds leaves and flowers up. It also carries water and sugars around the plant.

parts.name: Leaves
parts.fact: Leaves catch light. They use light, water and carbon dioxide to make sugar for the plant.

parts.name: Flower
parts.fact: A flower is the part that makes seeds in a flowering plant. It can attract animals that carry pollen.

parts.name: Fruit
parts.fact: A fruit forms from part of a flower and holds seeds. It can help protect or spread them.

parts.name: Seeds
parts.fact: A seed contains a tiny new plant and a food store. With the right conditions, it can begin to grow.

parts.name: Bud
parts.fact: A bud is a young shoot or flower before it opens. Its small leaves can protect the growing parts.

parts.name: Petal
parts.fact: Petals can attract animals that carry pollen with their colour, scent or shape.

parts.name: Sepal
parts.fact: Sepals protect the flower while it is a bud. They often look like small green leaves.

parts.name: Anther
parts.fact: The anther makes pollen. It sits at the top of a filament.

parts.name: Filament
parts.fact: The filament is a thin stalk. It holds the anther where pollen can be carried away.

parts.name: Stigma
parts.fact: The stigma receives pollen. Its surface is often sticky so pollen can stay there.

parts.name: Style
parts.fact: The style connects the stigma to the ovary. A pollen tube can grow down through it.

parts.name: Ovary
parts.fact: The ovary holds ovules. After fertilisation, the ovary can grow into a fruit.

parts.name: Ovule
parts.fact: An ovule contains an egg cell. After fertilisation, an ovule can develop into a seed.

topics.title: Parts of an Insect
topics.alt: Parts of an Insect painted learning picture

parts.name: Head
parts.fact: The head carries the eyes, antennae and mouthparts.

parts.name: Antennae
parts.fact: Antennae sense the world around the insect. They can detect touch and chemicals in the air.

parts.name: Compound eyes
parts.fact: A compound eye is made of many tiny units. Together they help the insect see movement and shapes.

parts.name: Mouthparts
parts.fact: Mouthparts are shaped for an insect’s food. Different insects bite, chew, suck or sip.

parts.name: Thorax
parts.fact: The thorax is the middle body section. All six legs attach to it.

parts.name: Six legs
parts.fact: Every adult insect has six jointed legs. The legs can be shaped for walking, jumping, digging or swimming.

parts.name: Wings
parts.fact: Many adult insects have wings attached to the thorax. Some insects have no wings.

parts.name: Abdomen
parts.fact: The abdomen is the rear body section. It holds the parts that digest food and help the insect lay eggs.

topics.title: Butterfly Life Cycle
topics.alt: Butterfly Life Cycle painted learning picture

parts.name: Egg
parts.fact: A butterfly begins as a tiny egg. The egg is usually laid on a plant the caterpillar can eat.

parts.name: Food plant
parts.fact: The food plant gives the new caterpillar its first meals. Different butterfly species need different plants.

parts.name: Caterpillar
parts.fact: The caterpillar, or larva, eats and grows. It sheds its skin as its body gets bigger.

parts.name: Chrysalis
parts.fact: Inside the chrysalis, the insect changes into its adult form. This change is called metamorphosis.

parts.name: Emerging butterfly
parts.fact: The adult comes out with soft, crumpled wings. It pumps fluid into them and waits while they become ready for flight.

parts.name: Adult butterfly
parts.fact: The adult drinks nectar for energy and can mate. A female can lay eggs, beginning the cycle again.

parts.name: Skull
parts.fact: The skull supports the face and protects the brain. It is made from several bones joined together.

parts.name: Jaw
parts.fact: The lower jaw moves when you talk and chew. It is the movable bone of the skull.

parts.name: Spine
parts.fact: The spine supports the head and body. Its vertebrae surround and protect the spinal cord.

parts.name: Ribs
parts.fact: The ribs form a flexible cage around the heart and lungs. They move a little as you breathe.

parts.name: Pelvis
parts.fact: The pelvis supports the body above the legs. It joins the spine to the hip joints.

parts.name: Humerus
parts.fact: The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm. It joins the shoulder to the elbow.

parts.name: Radius and ulna
parts.fact: The radius and ulna are the two forearm bones. Together they help the forearm and wrist turn.

parts.name: Hand bones
parts.fact: Each hand has many small bones. They let the wrist, palm and fingers make precise movements.

parts.name: Femur
parts.fact: The femur is the long thigh bone. It is the longest and strongest bone in the body.

parts.name: Tibia and fibula
parts.fact: The tibia and fibula are the two lower-leg bones. The tibia carries more of the body’s weight.

topics.title: Inside the Body
topics.alt: Inside the Body painted learning picture

parts.name: Brain
parts.fact: The brain receives information and directs many body activities. It helps you think, learn, remember and move.

parts.name: Lungs
parts.fact: The lungs bring oxygen from the air into the body. They also remove carbon dioxide when you breathe out.

parts.name: Heart
parts.fact: The heart is a strong muscle that pumps blood. Blood carries oxygen and other materials around the body.

parts.name: Stomach
parts.fact: The stomach stores and mixes food. Acid and enzymes begin breaking the food into smaller parts.

parts.name: Liver
parts.fact: The liver processes nutrients and helps remove harmful substances. It also makes bile for digestion.

parts.name: Small intestine
parts.fact: Most digestion and absorption of nutrients happens in the small intestine. Its long folded surface helps take nutrients into the blood.

parts.name: Large intestine
parts.fact: The large intestine absorbs water from what remains after digestion. It turns the waste into stool.

parts.name: Kidneys
parts.fact: The kidneys filter the blood and remove wastes and extra water. Those wastes leave the body as urine.

topics.title: Parts of a Fish
topics.alt: Parts of a Fish painted learning picture

parts.name: Mouth
parts.fact: Water can enter through the mouth and pass over the gills. The mouth also takes in food.

parts.name: Eye
parts.fact: A fish’s eyes help it find food, avoid danger and see its surroundings. Many fish can see colour.

parts.name: Gill cover
parts.fact: The gill cover protects the delicate gills of a bony fish. It also helps move water across them.

parts.name: Gills
parts.fact: Gills take oxygen from water. Blood carries that oxygen through the fish’s body.

parts.name: Dorsal fin
parts.fact: The dorsal fin is on the fish’s back. It helps many fish stay steady instead of rolling.

parts.name: Pectoral fins
parts.fact: Pectoral fins are paired fins near the front. They help many fish steer, brake and change depth.

parts.name: Tail fin
parts.fact: The tail fin pushes water to move the fish forward. It also helps the fish turn.

parts.name: Lateral line
parts.fact: The lateral line senses movement and vibration in the water. It helps a fish notice what is nearby.

topics.title: Parts of a Bird
topics.alt: Parts of a Bird painted learning picture

parts.name: Beak
parts.fact: A beak helps a bird pick up and eat food. Its shape often gives a clue about the bird’s diet.

parts.name: Eyes
parts.fact: Bird eyes help find food and watch for danger. Many birds can see colours very well.

parts.name: Wings
parts.fact: Wings are a bird’s front limbs. Most birds use them to fly, while penguins use theirs to swim.

parts.name: Flight feathers
parts.fact: The long feathers on the wings push against the air. They help provide lift and control in flight.

parts.name: Body feathers
parts.fact: Body feathers cover and protect the skin. They also trap air that helps keep the bird warm.

parts.name: Tail
parts.fact: The tail helps a flying bird steer, balance and slow down. It can also help a perched bird balance.

parts.name: Legs
parts.fact: A bird’s legs support it on the ground or a perch. Their shape suits the way the bird moves.

parts.name: Feet
parts.fact: Bird feet are shaped for different jobs, such as perching, swimming, scratching or catching prey.
